# Validation: bitter_grn_to_dng28.
name: bitter_grn_to_dng28
seed: 1000
flies: 5
warmup_s: 2
duration_s: 4
stimuli:
  - {at_s: 2.0, for_s: 2.0, target: bitter, mode: drive, amp: 0.5}

drug_cholinergic_block.yaml:
# 3.0 day 2, Pharmacology (MODEL PREDICTION): a 70% cholinergic block scales acetylcholine synapses to x0.3 (all predictions, however
# low their confidence). Compare with drug_picrotoxin.yaml. No receptor, kinetic or neuromodulatory model.
name: drug-cholinergic-block
seed: 100
flies: 3
warmup_s: 1
duration_s: 2
drug:
  doses: {cholinergic: 0.7}
recordings:
  - {name: whole_brain, neurons: "whole brain"}
  - {name: descending, neurons: "superclass:descending_neuron"}
drug_picrotoxin.yaml:
# 3.0 day 2, Pharmacology (MODEL PREDICTION): a 50% picrotoxin dose scales GABA and glutamate synapses to x0.5, leaving out
# low-confidence transmitter predictions (below 0.7). The effect is what the recurrent network does with less inhibition; the
# simulator's slow global gain pushes back, so read it soon after the drug goes on. A second file could use `cholinergic`.
name: drug-picrotoxin
seed: 100
flies: 3
warmup_s: 1
duration_s: 2
drug:
  doses: {picrotoxin: 0.5}
  include_low_confidence: false
  cut: 0.7
recordings:
  - {name: whole_brain, neurons: "whole brain"}
  - {name: descending, neurons: "superclass:descending_neuron"}
genetics_line_silencing.yaml:
# 3.0 day 2, Genetic toolkit: silence the neurons of a split-GAL4 driver line and look at the looming escape.
# SS00727 is listed for DNp01 (the giant fiber's descending neurons) in the split-GAL4 resource (Meissner et al. 2025, eLife,
# CC BY 4.0; Namiki et al. 2018 built the line). The table is LITERATURE; which neurons that selects here, and what silencing does,
# is the connectome and the model. Each seed also runs unperturbed as its control.
name: genetics-line-silencing
seed: 100
flies: 5
warmup_s: 2
duration_s: 3
surgery: {"line:SS00727": -1}
stimuli:
  - {at_s: 1.0, for_s: 1.0, target: loom, strength: 0.9, recruit: 0.6}
recordings:
  - {name: giant_fiber, neurons: "line:SS00727"}
  - {name: looming_detectors, neurons: loom}
imaging_looming.yaml:
# 3.0 day 2, Simulated calcium imaging (MODEL): GCaMP6f over the looming detectors, the giant fiber and every brain region while a
# looming stimulus drives LPLC2/LC4. Writes <seed>-imaging.csv (dF/F per ROI) next to the usual spike recordings; nwb: true adds an
# NWB file (RoiResponseSeries) and imaging.tiff: true a TIFF stack of the rendered brain view (slow: it builds the view).
name: imaging-looming
seed: 100
flies: 2
warmup_s: 2
duration_s: 4
stimuli:
  - {at_s: 1.0, for_s: 1.0, target: loom, strength: 0.9, recruit: 0.6}
imaging:
  indicator: gcamp6f
  fps: 20
  rois: ["type:LPLC2", "type:DNp01", "superclass:descending_neuron"]
recordings:
  - {name: giant_fiber, neurons: dnp01}

lecture_gf_lesion.yaml:
# Lecture Protocol: Giant Fiber Lesion: Visual vs Tactile Escape Pathways
# Demonstrates how DNp01 silencing abolishes looming visual escape while leaving tactile escape intact.
name: lecture-gf-lesion
title: "Giant Fiber Lesion: Visual vs Tactile Escape"
description: "Pedagogical walkthrough comparing visual looming vs mechanosensory escape under giant fiber lesion."
classroom: true
steps:
  - title: "1. Dual Parallel Escape Pathways"
    explanation: "Drosophila uses parallel escape pathways: fast visual escape via the giant fiber (DNp01), and tactile escape via antennal/leg mechanoreceptors through non-giant DNs."
    key_takeaway: "Parallel neural circuits mediate escape from looming shadows vs physical touch."
    citation: "von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962; Hampel et al. 2015, eLife 4:e08758"
    neurons:
      - label: "DNp01 (Giant Fiber)"
        spec: "dnp01"
        role: "Visual looming escape command"
      - label: "JO-C/E Mechanoreceptors"
        spec: "jo_ce"
        role: "Tactile air puff / touch detectors"
    action:
      kind: "reset"

  - title: "2. Silencing the Giant Fiber (DNp01 Lesion)"
    explanation: "Silencing DNp01 severs the direct link from looming detectors to thoracic jump motor neurons."
    key_takeaway: "DNp01 lesion selectively disables the visual looming escape circuit."
    citation: "von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962"
    neurons:
      - label: "DNp01 (Silenced)"
        spec: "dnp01"
        role: "Clamped silent (override 0.0)"
    action:
      kind: "surgery"
      target: "dnp01"
      mode: -1

  - title: "3. Looming Visual Cue (Fails)"
    explanation: "With DNp01 silenced, an optical looming stimulus excites LPLC2/LC4, but the signal cannot reach motor neurons. Escape jump fails."
    key_takeaway: "Visual looming stimuli fail to trigger escape when DNp01 is silenced."
    citation: "von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962"
    neurons:
      - label: "LPLC2 + LC4"
        spec: "type:LPLC2,LC4"
        role: "Active detectors blocked by severed DNp01"
    action:
      kind: "stimulus"
      target: "type:LPLC2,LC4"
      strength: 0.85
      for_s: 0.6

  - title: "4. Tactile Mechanosensory Cue (Preserved)"
    explanation: "Presenting tactile air puff / touch to antennae (JO-C/E) recruits alternative non-giant descending pathways. Tactile escape remains fully functional."
    key_takeaway: "Non-giant tactile escape pathways remain completely functional despite DNp01 ablation."
    citation: "Hampel et al. 2015, eLife 4:e08758; Allen et al. 2006, J Neurosci 26:1565"
    neurons:
      - label: "JO-C/E Mechanosensory"
        spec: "jo_ce"
        role: "Tactile sensory neurons"
      - label: "Alternative Descending Neurons"
        spec: "adn"
        role: "Intact tactile descending pathways"
    action:
      kind: "stimulus"
      target: "jo_ce"
      strength: 0.9
      for_s: 0.5
lecture_looming.yaml:
# Lecture Protocol: Looming Visual Escape Circuit
# Demonstrates how visual projection neurons LPLC2 and LC4 drive giant fiber DNp01.
name: lecture-looming
title: "Looming Visual Escape Circuit"
description: "Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila looming escape from retina to giant fiber."
classroom: true
steps:
  - title: "1. Spontaneous Baseline State"
    explanation: "Resting activity across optic lobe visual projection neurons and descending motor pathways is calm (~5-8 Hz baseline spontaneous firing). Inhibitory and excitatory inputs maintain homeostatic equilibrium."
    key_takeaway: "Baseline state is calm stochastic firing without premature escape trigger."
    citation: "von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962; Ache et al. 2019, Curr Biol 29:1073"
    neurons:
      - label: "LPLC2 + LC4"
        spec: "type:LPLC2,LC4"
        role: "Visual projection neurons sensitive to optical expansion"
      - label: "DNp01 (Giant Fiber)"
        spec: "dnp01"
        role: "Descending escape command neuron"
    action:
      kind: "reset"

  - title: "2. Expanding Retinal Loom Detection"
    explanation: "An approaching threat expands on the retina. LPLC2 and LC4 compute non-linear angular expansion rates and fire high-frequency action potentials."
    key_takeaway: "LPLC2 and LC4 selectively encode optical looming expansion."
    citation: "Ache et al. 2019, Curr Biol 29:1073"
    neurons:
      - label: "LPLC2, LC4"
        spec: "type:LPLC2,LC4"
        role: "Visual detectors driven by looming edge expansion"
    action:
      kind: "stimulus"
      target: "type:LPLC2,LC4"
      strength: 0.85
      for_s: 0.6

  - title: "3. Synaptic Convergence onto Giant Fiber"
    explanation: "LPLC2 and LC4 terminate directly in the posterior slope, forming hundreds of chemical synapses onto giant dendrites of descending neuron DNp01."
    key_takeaway: "Summation of hundreds of inputs rapidly depolarizes DNp01 toward firing threshold."
    citation: "von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962"
    neurons:
      - label: "DNp01"
        spec: "dnp01"
        role: "Giant fiber receiving posterior slope synaptic convergence"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "type:LPLC2,LC4"
      amp: 0.65
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "4. Escape Jump Motor Readout"
    explanation: "Once DNp01 fires, its action potential propagates down the cervical connective into the thoracic ganglion, activating tergotrochanteral motor neurons."
    key_takeaway: "DNp01 activation triggers an unguided, explosive jump takeoff in <5 ms."
    citation: "von Reyn et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:962; Allen et al. 2006, J Neurosci 26:1565"
    neurons:
      - label: "DNp01"
        spec: "dnp01"
        role: "Descending command trigger"
      - label: "Leg Motor Neurons"
        spec: "mn_legs"
        role: "Thoracic jump motor pool"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "dnp01"
      amp: 1.0
      for_s: 0.4
lecture_moonwalker.yaml:
# Lecture Protocol: Moonwalker Backward Walking Circuit
# Demonstrates how Moonwalker Descending Neurons (MDN) coordinate reversal of leg motor rhythms.
name: lecture-moonwalker
title: "Moonwalker Backward Walking Circuit"
description: "Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila backward walking coordination by MDN."
classroom: true
steps:
  - title: "1. Forward Walking Default State"
    explanation: "In foraging flies, descending neurons like DNp09 promote forward walking, driving tripod leg motor patterns."
    key_takeaway: "Forward locomotion is driven by forward-promoting descending command neurons."
    citation: "Bidaye et al. 2014, Science 344:97; Bidaye et al. 2020, Neuron 108:109"
    neurons:
      - label: "DNp09 (Forward DN)"
        spec: "type:DNp09"
        role: "Promotes forward walking"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "type:DNp09"
      amp: 0.6
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "2. Collision & MDN Activation"
    explanation: "Physical obstacles or mechanosensory antennal touch activate the bilateral pair of Moonwalker Descending Neurons (MDN)."
    key_takeaway: "Obstacle collision rapidly excites MDN command neurons."
    citation: "Bidaye et al. 2014, Science 344:97"
    neurons:
      - label: "MDN"
        spec: "mdn"
        role: "Bilateral descending neurons directing backward walking"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "mdn"
      amp: 0.8
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "3. Stepping Rhythm Inversion"
    explanation: "MDN simultaneously inhibits forward walking central pattern generators and activates backward motor rhythms, inverting stepping phase."
    key_takeaway: "MDN acts as an executive toggle switching gait polarity."
    citation: "Bidaye et al. 2014, Science 344:97; Feng et al. 2020, Nature 585:395"
    neurons:
      - label: "MDN & Thoracic Motor Pools"
        spec: "mn_legs"
        role: "Reverse leg phase coordination"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "mdn"
      amp: 1.0
      for_s: 0.6
lecture_sugar.yaml:
# Lecture Protocol: Sugar Gustatory Pathway & Proboscis Extension
# Demonstrates how sweet gustatory neurons project via SEL PNs to motor neuron MN9.
name: lecture-sugar
title: "Sugar Gustatory Pathway & Proboscis Extension"
description: "Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila sugar taste sensing and feeding reflex."
classroom: true
steps:
  - title: "1. Gustatory Detection by Sugar Receptors"
    explanation: "Sucrose contact excites gustatory receptor neurons (GRNs) on labellum and tarsi, sending action potentials into the subesophageal zone."
    key_takeaway: "Sugar contact activates gustatory sensory neurons innervating the SEZ."
    citation: "Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210; Yao & Scott 2022, Cell 185:2472"
    neurons:
      - label: "Sugar Gustatory Neurons"
        spec: "sweet"
        role: "Sensory detection of sweet tastants"
    action:
      kind: "stimulus"
      target: "sweet"
      strength: 0.8
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "2. Relay via Sugar SEL Projection Neurons"
    explanation: "Sugar sensory afferents synapse onto subesophageal layer projection neurons (Sugar SEL PNs: GNG540/GNG550), relaying excitation to motor command pools."
    key_takeaway: "Sugar SEL PNs relay taste signals to feeding motor circuits."
    citation: "Yao & Scott 2022, Cell 185:2472; Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210"
    neurons:
      - label: "Sugar SEL PNs"
        spec: "type:GNG540,GNG550"
        role: "Second-order gustatory relay neurons"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "type:GNG540,GNG550"
      amp: 0.7
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "3. Motor Neuron 9 (MN9) Proboscis Extension"
    explanation: "Excitatory signals reach MN9, innervating the retractor bulbi muscle to trigger the Proboscis Extension Response (PER). Bitter taste pathways do not excite MN9."
    key_takeaway: "MN9 drives proboscis extension; bitter inputs fail to activate MN9."
    citation: "Shiu et al. 2024, Nature 634:210; Schwarz et al. 2017, eLife 6:e19892"
    neurons:
      - label: "MN9"
        spec: "mn9"
        role: "Proboscis extension motor neuron"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "sweet"
      amp: 0.9
      for_s: 0.5
lecture_tmaze.yaml:
# Lecture Protocol: Mushroom Body Olfactory Conditioning
# Demonstrates dopamine-gated depression of KC-to-MBON synapses in learned odor avoidance.
name: lecture-tmaze
title: "Mushroom Body Olfactory Conditioning"
description: "Pedagogical walkthrough of Drosophila olfactory associative learning in the mushroom body."
classroom: true
steps:
  - title: "1. Sparse Odor Encoding by Kenyon Cells"
    explanation: "Antennal lobe projection neurons diverge onto ~2,000 intrinsic Kenyon Cells (KCs). Odors activate sparse, decorrelated ~5% subsets of KCs in the mushroom body calyx."
    key_takeaway: "Kenyon cells form sparse, distinct odor representations."
    citation: "Aso et al. 2014, eLife 3:e04577; Turner et al. 2008, Nature 454:493"
    neurons:
      - label: "Kenyon Cells"
        spec: "prefix:KC"
        role: "Sparse intrinsic odor representation"
    action:
      kind: "stimulus"
      target: "odor_a"
      strength: 0.7
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "2. Dopaminergic Reinforcement (PPL1 / Electric Shock)"
    explanation: "Pairing CS+ odor with electric shock recruits PPL1 dopaminergic neurons, releasing dopamine coincident with active Kenyon cell presynaptic boutons."
    key_takeaway: "PPL1 DANs signal negative reinforcement to specific mushroom body compartments."
    citation: "Claridge-Chang et al. 2009, Cell 139:405; Aso et al. 2014, eLife 3:e04577"
    neurons:
      - label: "PPL1 Dopaminergic Neurons"
        spec: "type:PPL101,PPL103"
        role: "Aversive dopamine reinforcement"
    action:
      kind: "drive"
      target: "type:PPL101,PPL103"
      amp: 0.8
      for_s: 0.5

  - title: "3. Long-Term Depression at KC-to-MBON Synapses"
    explanation: "Coincident KC spikes and dopamine drive selective long-term depression (LTD) of synapses from active KCs onto approach-directing MBONs."
    key_takeaway: "LTD of approach MBONs tips circuit balance toward avoidance."
    citation: "Hige et al. 2015, Neuron 88:985; Owald & Waddell 2015, Curr Opin Neurobiol 35:178"
    neurons:
      - label: "Mushroom Body Output Neurons"
        spec: "mbon"
        role: "Readout neurons projecting to motor systems"
    action:
      kind: "assay_step"
      target: "tmaze_condition"

  - title: "4. Memory Recall & T-Maze Choice"
    explanation: "At the choice point, CS+ odor evokes depressed approach MBON firing. Unbalanced avoidance signals steer the fly into the safe odor arm."
    key_takeaway: "Flies avoid the shock-paired odor with statistically significant avoidance (PI > 0.5)."
    citation: "Tully & Quinn 1985, J Comp Physiol A 157:263"
    neurons:
      - label: "MBONs (Approach vs Avoidance)"
        spec: "mbon"
        role: "Differential population steering"
    action:
      kind: "stimulus"
      target: "odor_a"
      strength: 0.8
      for_s: 0.5

optomotor.yaml:

# T4b/T5b_L back-to-front on the left), recording the steering neurons on both sides. amp 0.5 is what the EMD stage

seed: 1000
flies: 5
warmup_s: 2
duration_s: 4
stimuli:
  - {at_s: 2.0, for_s: 2.0, target: optomotor_right, mode: drive, amp: 0.5}

  - {name: dna_steer_r, neurons: dna_steer_r}

orchard-feeding.yaml:
# Orchard feeding, headless and reproducible: one fly feeds on the Orchard's fruit for two minutes.
# The fruit, how many feeds each holds, regrowth and the fly's fly-feed-fly schedule are game rules
# (kickthefly/game/outdoors.py); feeding drives the real sugar-pathway taste and PAM reward neurons.
# Readouts: MN9 and PAM firing while feeding vs travelling, feeds, fruit emptied.
name: orchard-feeding
assay: orchard
seed: 4000
flies: 4
assay_options: {feeds: 4, regrow_s: 75, cap: 4, duration_s: 120}
patch_dnp01_if_curve.yaml:
# 3.0 day 2, Virtual patch clamp (MODEL: a point-neuron LIF unit, NOT electrophysiology; potential and current are in model units).
# Current-clamp the first DNp01 neuron of each fly and record firing rate against injected current, with the synaptic input of the
# wired brain (embedded) and with none (isolated: the same unit in every neuron).
name: patch-dnp01-if-curve
seed: 100
flies: 3
patch:
  neuron: "type:DNp01"
  index: 0
  mode: embedded
  amplitudes: [0.0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5]
  duration_ms: 500
  repeats: 3
  warmup_s: 2
predator_escape_assay.yaml:
# 3.0 day 3, Predators: escape probability by predator (labjobs "predator_escape"). Each fly faces the frog, the dragonfly and the
# mantis 3 times; an escape is the game's own rule (DNp01 above 4x its calm rate before the capture). The attacks are game rules and
# the probabilities are MODEL PREDICTIONS. Validation seeds 1000-1009; pass criteria are in kickthefly/lab/predators.py (CRITERIA),
# written before the first run.
name: predator-escape-assay
assay: predator_escape
seed: 1000
flies: 10
assay_options:
  trials: 3
predator_mantis_creep.yaml:
# 3.0 day 3, Predators: one mantis attack as looming onto LPLC2/LC4 (game/predators.py). The slow creep stays below the looming threshold and
# the strike does not: compare the loom group before and after the strike. The attack is a game rule; the response is the connectome's.
name: predator-mantis-creep
seed: 1000
flies: 2
warmup_s: 1
duration_s: 14
predator: {kind: mantis, at_s: 0.5}
recordings:
  - {name: looming detectors, neurons: "loom"}
  - {name: giant fiber, neurons: "dnp01"}
rig_ball.yaml:
# 3.0 day 5: a fly on a ball with a virtual-reality world driven by the ball (game/rigs.py). Turning from DNa01/02, walking from DNp09
# (CONNECTOME); ball, VR and bar (a distant landmark, tracked by LC10 through the duel's rule) are GAME RULE. mode: open freezes the VR.
name: rig-ball
seed: 0
flies: 1
rig: {name: ball, mode: closed, scene: bar, seconds: 30, bar_deg: 90}
rig_buridan.yaml:
# 3.0 day 5: Buridan's paradigm (game/rigs.py): a round platform, two opposite stripes beyond its edge, the walking trajectory recorded. Steering
# and speed are read from DNa01/02 and DNp09 (CONNECTOME). GAME RULE: the platform, the edge reflection, one stripe tracked at a time (LC10),
# the definitions of stripe deviation and transits. mode: none is the no-stripe control. Pre-registered assay: --rig-assay buridan.
name: rig-buridan
seed: 0
flies: 1
rig: {name: buridan, mode: stripes, seconds: 60}
rig_fourfield.yaml:
# 3.0 day 5: the four-field olfactory arena (game/rigs.py): four quadrants, one odor in two opposite ones, preference index from the time spent.
# The odor drives the olfactory receptor neurons of the game's own scent poke (CONNECTOME); the arena, its sharp quadrant boundaries and the PI
# definition are GAME RULE. mode: sham delivers no odor (the control). Nothing in the model gives the fly a reason to prefer or avoid an odor
# except what the wiring does with it: report what happens. Pre-registered assay: --rig-assay fourfield.
name: rig-fourfield
seed: 0
flies: 1
rig: {name: fourfield, mode: odor, seconds: 60}
rig_tethered.yaml:
# 3.0 day 5: the tethered flight simulator (game/rigs.py). The fly is fixed; the panorama around it rotates to the right, rests, then to the
# left. CONNECTOME: yaw from DNa01 + DNa02 right minus left; the rotation reaches them through T4/T5 (validated: optomotor_turning).
# GAME RULE: the EMD stage, the yaw gain, the panorama. mode: closed also rotates the panorama by the fly's own yaw. MODEL PREDICTION: the response.
name: rig-tethered
seed: 0
flies: 1
rig: {name: tethered, mode: open, omega: 3.0, seconds: 14}
selftest_smoke.yaml:
# The 10-second headless smoke protocol `--selftest` runs (Settings > Help > Run self-test does the same). Ten seconds
# of simulated time: a calm stretch, the looming detectors driven for two seconds, calm again. The self-test checks the
# detectors fired while driven and that nothing raised.
name: selftest_smoke
seed: 7
flies: 1
warmup_s: 0.5
duration_s: 10
stimuli:
  - {at_s: 3.0, for_s: 2.0, target: loom, mode: drive, amp: 0.5}
recordings:
  - {name: giant_fiber, neurons: dnp01}
  - {name: looming_detectors, neurons: loom}
sleep_deprivation_assay.yaml:
# 3.0 day 4: the sleep deprivation assay as a protocol (labjobs "sleep_deprivation"). Each seed is its own control (a paired design,
# so no surgery). GAME RULE: sleep pressure, the disturbances, what counts as sleep. CONNECTOME: the dFB (FB6/FB7) firing it drives.
# MODEL PREDICTION: the rebound. Validation seeds 1000-1009; the pass criteria are in kickthefly/lab/sleepdep.py, written before the
# first run. About two minutes of simulated time per fly and condition: shorten the windows for a quick look.
name: sleep-deprivation-assay
assay: sleep_deprivation
seed: 1000
flies: 10
assay_options:
  deprive_s: 45
  recover_s: 60
  mode: "off"
smoke.yaml:
# The build check CI runs on the exe and the AppImage: loads the brain pack, runs 1 s of sim and drives the looming
# detectors. Quick (a few seconds after the brain loads).
name: smoke
seed: 1
flies: 1
warmup_s: 0.5
